## Axis convention

All segment coordinate systems follow one right-handed convention. In the anatomical position (upright stance, arms at the sides, palms facing forward), X points to the subject's right, Y anteriorly and Z superiorly. For each axis, the landmark that defines 0 % and the landmark that defines 100 % are chosen so that the axis points in this direction. If the limits of an axis are exchanged, coordinates on that axis convert as u_new = 100 − u_old.

Each axis is written as `A (0 %) → B (100 %)`: the axis points from the 0 % landmark A to the 100 % landmark B. See the [formal definition](index.qmd#formal-definition) for how coordinates are computed.

NOTE: Joint markers should be annotated in the same coordinate system as their proximal body part. For example, the right shoulder joint marker should be annotated in the same coordinate system as torso, and the right elbow joint marker should be annotated in the same coordinate system as the right upper-arm.
